digest.component_or_area: DC outbound differ, text sanitization and convergence
propositions: DC lacks convergence test suites for comment and description length truncation, while Cloud has two such suites that prevent re-emission of truncated values on round-trip
The DC comment sanitizer incorrectly reuses the description fitter constant WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32767), creating coupling risk despite being correct for the current text format
A comment-convergence test driven through compute_outbound_mutations silently resolves DC's sanitizer via config fallback, causing it to measure against Cloud's truncation path instead of DC's
A description-convergence test requires explicit injection of all three of outbound_mapper, inbound_mapper, and links; injecting only one still fires the OR-guarded fallback to Cloud

The 32767 character ceiling for both comments and descriptions is the documented default of jira.text.field.character.limit (jpm.xml, JRASERVER-28519), not an assumption, and must be cited at the binding

DC convergence tests must prove they exercised DC's path via identity/recording checks for comments and value-based discriminators for descriptions, not value assertions that pass under either backend
